messages.text: I'm buying my first proper chef's knife. Looking at the Wüsthof Classic versus the Shun Classic versus the Misono UX10. Help me pick.

Different philosophies:

- **Wüsthof Classic** is a German workhorse — heavier, full bolster, very durable, more forgiving of poor cutting board choice. Sharpens easily, holds an edge for months of normal home use.
- **Shun Classic** is Japanese-styled but made for Western markets — lighter, sharper out of the box, with a wood-grain Damascus pattern. Beautiful, but the edge can chip if you hit bone.
- **Misono UX10** is the real-deal pro-favorite Japanese knife. Razor sharp, holds an edge longer than the others, but it's an investment and you need to baby it.

For a first nice knife: Wüsthof if you want low-maintenance. Misono if you're committed to learning sharpening and care. Shun is somewhere in the middle.
Going with the Wüsthof. By the way — wholly unrelated thread — I have an egg allergy, just want it in your context for any future food questions.
Got the egg allergy noted. Good Wüsthof choice — they'll last decades with basic care.
